source_text: Ἐὰν ἐντύχῃς νεωτέρῳ καταπονουμένῳ, οὕτω δάκρυσον, ὡς ἐκεῖνος τὸν Βεν ιαμὶν τὸν τοῦ γήρως υἱόν. Πειράζει καὶ σὲ τυχὸν ἡ πλεονεξία, ὡς τὸν Ἰωσὴφ ἡ δέσποινα· ἕλκει σε τῶν ἱματίων, ἵνα τῆς ἐντολῆς καταφρονήσῃς, καὶ φιλήσῃς μᾶλλον ἐκείνην τὴν φιλόχρυσον καὶ φιλόκοσμον παρὰ τὸ τοῦ Δεσπότου πρόσταγμα. Ὅταν δὴ ἔλθῃ λογισμὸς τῇ ἐντολῇ ἐκείνῃ πολεμῶν, καὶ τὸν σώφρονα νοῦν εἰς τὴν φιλαργυρίαν ἐπισπώμενος, τῆς φιλαδελφίας καταναγκάζων ἀμελεῖν, καὶ κατ έχων πρὸς αὐτὴν, πρόσριψον καὶ σὺ τὰ ἱμάτια, ὀργι σθεὶς ἀναχώρησον· φύλαξον τῷ Κυρίῳ τὴν πίστιν, ὡς ἐκεῖνος τῷ Πεντεφρῇ· ἐν ἑνὶ ἐνιαυτῷ τὴν ἔνδειαν οἰκονόμησον, ὡς ἐκεῖνος ἐν τοῖς ἑπτά. Μὴ τὰ πάντα τῇ ἡδονῇ, δός τι καὶ τῇ ψυχῇ. Καὶ δύο σοι νόμισον εἶναι θυγατέρας· τὴν εὐπάθειαν τὴν ἐνθάδε, καὶ τὴν ζωὴν τὴν ἐν τοῖς οὐρανοῖς. Εἰ μὴ θελήσῃς τὰ πάντα δοῦναι τῇ κρείττονι, μέρισον γοῦν ἐξ ἴσης τῇ τε ἀκολάστῳ παιδὶ καὶ τῇ σώφρονι. Μὴ τὴν ἐνταῦθα διαγω γὴν ὑπέρπλουτον δείξῃς, γυμνὴν δὲ τὴν ἄλλην καὶ ῥακίοις ἠμφιεσμένην, ἡνίκα ἂν δέῃ σε τῷ Χριστῷ παραστῆναι, καὶ εἰς ὄψιν ἐλθεῖν τοῦ κριτοῦ, νύμφης ἔχουσαν σχῆμα, καὶ κλῆσιν τὴν κατ' ἀρετὴν ζωήν. Μὴ τοίνυν ἄμορφον καὶ ἄκοσμον παρα στήσῃς τῷ νυμφίῳ τὴν νύμφην, ἵνα μὴ θεασάμενος ἀποκλίνῃ τὸ πρόσωπον, καὶ ἰδὼν μισήσῃ, καὶ τὴν συνάφειαν ἀπαρνήσηται. Ἀλλὰ στείλας αὐτὴν τῷ προσήκοντι κόσμῳ, τήρησον εὔμορφον τῇ προθεσμίᾳ τῶν γάμων· ἵνα καὶ αὐτὴ μετὰ τῶν φρονίμων παρθένων ἀνάψῃ τὴν λαμπάδα, ἔχουσα τὸ πῦρ τῆς γνώσεως ἄσβεστον, καὶ μὴ λείπουσα τῶν κατορθωμάτων τὸ ἔλαιον· ἵν' ἔργοις ἡ θεοφορουμένη προφητεία βεβαιωθῇ, ἐφαρμόσῃ δὲ καὶ τῇ σῇ ψυχῇ τὸ λεχθέν· Παρέστη ἡ βασίλισσα ἐκ δεξιῶν σου, ἐν ἱματισμῷ διαχρύσῳ περιβεβλημένη, πεποικιλμένη. Ἄκουσον, θύγατερ, καὶ ἴδε, καὶ κλῖνον τὸ οὖς σου, καὶ ἐπιθυμήσει ὁ βασιλεὺς τοῦ κάλλους σου. Ταῦτα γὰρ γενικῶς προανεφώνησεν ὁ Ψαλμῳδὸς, τοῦ γενικοῦ σώματος προκηρύσσων τὴν ὥραν· ἐφαρμόσει δὲ κυρίως καὶ τῇ ἑκάστου ψυχῇ, εἴπερ ἐκ τῶν καθ' ἕκαστον ἔχει ἡ Ἐκκλησία τὸ σύστημα. Προνόησόν μοι λογικῶς τὸ παρὸν καὶ τὸ μέλλον, ὃ μὴ διὰ κέρδος αἰσχρὸν προδῷς. Καταλείψει σε σῶμα, τὸ σὸν γνώρισμα τῷ βίῳ. Εἰς δὴ τὴν ἐπιφάνειαν τοῦ προσδοκωμένου κριτοῦ, καὶ ἀναμφιβόλως ἥξοντος, ἀποκλείσεις μὲν σεαυτῷ τὴν τῶν τιμῶν δόσιν καὶ τὴν ἐπουράνιον δόξαν, ἀνοίξεις δὲ πῦρ ἄσβεστον, καὶ γέενναν, καὶ κολαστήρια, καὶ πικροὺς ἐν ὀδύναις αἰῶνας, ἀντὶ μακρᾶς καὶ μακαρίας ζωῆς. Μή με νομίσῃς, ὥσπερ μητέρα τινὰ ἢ τροφὸν, ψευδῆ σοι μορμολύκεια ἐπισείειν, ὥσπερ ἐκεῖναι ποιεῖν περὶ τοὺς νηπίους τῶν παίδων εἰώθασιν· ὅταν θρηνῶσιν ἄτακτα καὶ ἀπέραντα, δι' ἐπι-πλάστων διηγημάτων κατασιγάζουσιν. Ταῦτα δὲ οὐ μῦθος, ἀλλὰ λόγος ἀψευδεῖ προκεκηρυγμένος φωνῇ. Καὶ ἴσθι γε ἀκριβῶς κατὰ τὴν εὐαγγελικὴν πρόῤῥησιν, ἰῶτα ἓν ἢ μία κεραία οὐ μὴ παρέλθῃ. Ἀλλὰ καὶ σῶμα τὸ ἐν θήκαις ἀφανισθὲν ἀναστήσε-ται, καὶ ψυχὴ ἡ αὐτὴ ἡ τῷ θανάτῳ ἀποκλεισθεῖσα, πάλιν ἐνοικήσει τῷ σώματι. Καὶ τῶν βεβιωμένων ἔλεγχος ἀκριβὴς παραστήσεται, οὐκ ἄλλων μαρτυρούντων, ἀλλ' αὐτῆς μαρτυρούσης τῆς συνειδήσεως. Ἑκάστῳ δὲ τὰ πρὸς ἀξίαν παρὰ τοῦ δικαίου κριτοῦ ἀντιμετρηθήσεται. Αὐτῷ πρέπει δόξα, κράτος καὶ προσκύνησις, εἰς τοὺς αἰῶνας τῶν αἰώνων. Ἀμήν.
thought_title: The soul as bride prepared for Christ
orientation: Basil is closing the homily, urging each hearer to resist greed and to prepare the soul as a bride for Christ at the coming judgment.
pass_a_gloss: If you meet a younger man being worn down, weep in this way, as that man wept for Benjamin, the son of his old age. Greed perhaps also tests you, as the mistress tested Joseph; she drags you by the clothes, so that you may despise the commandment and love rather that gold-loving and ornament-loving woman instead of the Master's command. Whenever then a reasoning comes warring against that commandment, and drawing the chaste mind toward love of money, forcing it to neglect love for one another, and holding you toward it, throw off also you the clothes, become angry and withdraw; keep faith with the Lord, as that man kept it with Pentephres; manage the want in one year, as that man managed it in seven. Do not give everything to pleasure; give something also to the soul. Consider also that you have two daughters: the luxury here, and the life in the heavens. If you are not willing to give everything to the better one, divide at least equally between the licentious girl and the chaste one. Do not show the life here as exceedingly rich, but the other one naked and clothed in rags, when it is necessary for you to stand before Christ and to come into the sight of the judge, having the form of a bride, and as its title the life according to virtue. Do not then present the bride to the bridegroom shapeless and unadorned, so that he may not, seeing her, turn away his face, and seeing her, hate her, and refuse the union. But having arrayed her with fitting adornment, keep her beautiful for the appointed time of the wedding; so that she also with the wise virgins may light the lamp, having the fire of knowledge unquenchable, and not lacking the oil of good deeds; so that by deeds the God-borne prophecy may be confirmed, and the saying may fit also your soul: The queen stood at your right hand, clothed in gold-woven raiment, embroidered. Hear, daughter, and see, and incline your ear, and the king will desire your beauty. For these things the Psalmist proclaimed beforehand in general, proclaiming beforehand the beauty of the general body; and it will fit properly also the soul of each one, if indeed the Church has its constitution from the individuals. Provide for me rationally the present and the future, which you may not betray for shameful gain. The body will leave you, your distinguishing mark in life. At the appearing of the expected judge, who will certainly come, you will shut out for yourself the giving of rewards and the heavenly glory, and you will open unquenchable fire, and Gehenna, and places of punishment, and bitter ages in pains, instead of long and blessed life. Do not think that I, like some mother or nurse, am brandishing false bogey-figures at you, as those women are accustomed to do with infant children; when they wail disorderly and endlessly, they quiet them with made-up stories. But these things are not a myth, but a word proclaimed beforehand with a truthful voice. And know precisely according to the gospel prediction, one iota or one tittle will not pass away. But also the body destroyed in tombs will rise, and the same soul confined by death will again dwell in the body. And an exact examination of the things lived will be presented, not with others testifying, but with the conscience itself testifying. And to each one the things according to worth will be measured out by the just judge. To him is fitting glory, might and worship, to the ages of ages. Amen.

choices.term: τὸν Βενιαμὶν τὸν τοῦ γήρως υἱόν
choices.english: Benjamin, the son of his old age
choices.why: The phrase specifies Jacob's son Benjamin as the child of Jacob's old age; 'his' is implied by the context of Joseph weeping for Benjamin.
rejected: Benjamin, the son of old age

choices.why: κατέχω with πρός means 'hold toward, draw toward'; the reasoning holds the mind toward greed, not back from it.
εὐπάθεια in this moral context means indulgence or luxurious living, pejorative, not neutral comfort.
rejected: the comfort of this life here

choices.why: παιδί here refers to one of the two daughters in the metaphor; ἀκόλαστος means wanton or licentious.
τιμαί in eschatological context means rewards or prizes, not honors in the sense of respect.
ἀποκλείω means 'shut in, confine'; the soul is shut in by death, not shut out.
rejected: the soul shut out by death

pass_b_english: If you meet a younger man who is worn down, weep for him as Joseph wept for Benjamin, the son of his old age. Perhaps greed is testing you too, as the mistress tested Joseph. It pulls at your clothes, so that you will despise the commandment and love that gold-loving, ornament-loving woman more than the Master's order. So when a thought comes to fight against that commandment, drawing your chaste mind toward love of money, forcing you to neglect love for one another and holding you toward it, throw off your clothes too, and leave in anger. Keep faith with the Lord, as Joseph kept faith with Pentephres, the Egyptian master. Manage the want in one year, as he managed it in seven. Do not give everything to pleasure; give something to the soul as well. Consider that you have two daughters: the luxury here, and the life in the heavens. If you are not willing to give everything to the better one, at least divide equally between the licentious girl and the chaste one. Do not make your life here extravagantly rich while the other is naked and dressed in rags, when you must stand before Christ and come into the sight of the Judge, having the form of a bride and the name of a life according to virtue. Do not present the bride to the bridegroom shapeless and unadorned, so that when he sees her he does not turn his face away, and when he looks he does not hate her and refuse the union. Instead, dress her in fitting adornment and keep her beautiful for the appointed time of the wedding, so that she too may light her lamp with the wise virgins, having the unquenchable fire of knowledge and not lacking the oil of good deeds. So that the God-inspired prophecy may be confirmed by deeds, and what was said may apply to your soul: “The queen stood at your right hand, clothed in gold-woven garments, richly adorned. Hear, daughter, and see, and incline your ear, and the king will desire your beauty” (Psalm 45:9-11). For the Psalmist proclaimed these things in general, announcing beforehand the beauty of the whole body; but it will apply properly to each individual soul, since the Church is made up of individuals. Provide for me rationally for the present and the future, which you should not betray for shameful gain. A body will leave you, your distinguishing mark in life. At the appearing of the expected Judge, who will certainly come, you will shut yourself out from the granting of rewards and the heavenly glory, and you will open unquenchable fire, and Gehenna, and punishments, and bitter ages in anguish, instead of long and blessed life. Do not think that I am shaking false bogeymen at you, as some mother or nurse does; they are accustomed to do this with infant children when they cry without order and without end, silencing them with made-up stories. But these things are not a myth, but a word proclaimed beforehand by a voice that does not lie. And know precisely, according to the Gospel prediction, not one iota or one stroke will pass away (Matthew 5:18). But the body that has vanished in the tombs will rise, and the same soul that was confined by death will dwell in the body again. And an exact examination of what has been lived will be presented, with no others testifying, but the conscience itself testifying. To each one, what is deserved will be measured out by the just Judge. To him belong glory, power, and worship, to the ages of ages. Amen.

problems.quote: weep for him as Joseph wept for Benjamin
problems.source_quote: οὕτω δάκρυσον, ὡς ἐκεῖνος τὸν Βενιαμὶν τὸν τοῦ γήρως υἱόν
problems.why: Source says 'weep as he [Joseph] wept for Benjamin,' but English omits 'as he' and makes Joseph the subject of weeping twice, losing the parallel structure.
problems.fix: weep for him as he wept for Benjamin, the son of his old age.

problems.why: Work brief names 'Pentephres' as 'the Egyptian master to whom Joseph was faithful, traditionally identified with Potiphar.' English uses generic 'Egyptian master,' losing the specific name and the allusion to Genesis narrative.
τιμῶν means 'honors' or 'glories,' not 'rewards' in a material sense; this weakens the eschatological dignity language.

problems.quote: Manage the want in one year, as Joseph managed it in seven.
problems.source_quote: ἐν ἑνὶ ἐνιαυτῷ τὴν ἔνδειαν οἰκονόμησον, ὡς ἐκεῖνος ἐν τοῖς ἑπτά.
problems.why: Source says manage want in ONE year as Joseph did in SEVEN; English reverses the comparison's force.
problems.fix: Manage the want in one year, as he managed it in seven.
problems.ruling: Source: manage want in ONE year as Joseph in SEVEN. English reverses to 'in one year...as Joseph...in seven'—but 'it' refers to 'want,' so Joseph managed want in seven, you in one. English garbles: 'Manage the want in one year, as Joseph managed it in seven' actually matches source structure; re-reading, English says same. Wait: 'Manage the want in one year, as Joseph managed it in seven'—this matches source exactly. Claim is wrong; no reversal. English is correct.

problems.quote: Provide for me rationally for the present and the future
problems.source_quote: Προνόησόν μοι λογικῶς τὸ παρὸν καὶ τὸ μέλλον
problems.why: Source says 'provide rationally for the present and the future'; 'for me' is an error—dative 'μοι' is ethical dative, not recipient.
problems.fix: Provide rationally for the present and the future
problems.ruling: μοι is ethical dative ('for yourself,' 'on your part'), not 'for me.' English 'Provide for me' makes speaker the beneficiary; source has no such recipient. Changes meaning significantly.
